name: Coleman Bridge, Singapore
facts: Coleman Bridge, designed by Irish architect George Drumgoole Coleman, first opened in 1840 as a nine‑arch brick structure linking Old Bridge Road and Hill Street over the Singapore River.
In 1886, the original timber span was replaced by an iron bridge, celebrated as one of the most attractive river crossings until its demolition in 1984 to accommodate widening.

The 1987 concrete replacement preserved historic iron lamp posts and railings, honoring the bridge’s heritage while improving traffic flow for the next fifteen years before the North East MRT line opened.
